issues.explanation: The invite e-mail field has no `@error('inviteEmail')`; the old form rendered `@error('email')` explicitly and this one delegates entirely to `x-input`. Unless `x-input` renders the message itself, `sendInvite` errors are invisible (zero `help is-danger`) and the 'renders exactly once' requirement (and the test at `MembersTest.php` - 'a validation error on the invite e-mail renders exactly once') fails.

`openMember()` authorizes the `update` ability on an `EntityMembership`, but this diff adds no such ability and the old code only used `assignRole`/`delete`; if `EntityMembershipPolicy` has no `update` method, Gate denies it and every manager gets 403, so the member modal never opens.

Invite creation, cancellation, acceptance/decline and role changes are domain writes performed inline in Livewire components; `conventions.md` requires one `app/Actions/*` class per use case with authorization inside the action.

No `entity.members` route change is included; manager-only access relies only on the component mount. That produces 403 when the route renders the component, but the route itself still has no owner/admin guard as the requirement asks.

`saveRole()` validates `memberRole` before resolving the target and checking ownership, so submitting the owner's membership with its unchanged `'owner'` draft returns a validation error on `memberRole` instead of the specified 403; only an admin/employee draft reaches the immutability check.

Accept/decline authorization is an inline `abort_unless(..., 403)` rather than a policy/gate, contrary to 'authorization always goes through policies/gates'; a dedicated invite policy should own the invitee check.

`selectedMembershipId` is a client-writable record ID without `#[Locked]`, contrary to the Livewire rule for server-only IDs; impact is limited because `saveRole()`/`render()` re-resolve it through the entity, but it should be locked and the tamper test should not rely on setting it.

`confirmRemoval()`, `cancelRemoval()` and `closeMember()` are public actions with no server-side authorization; impact is low (they only toggle modal state and `removeMember()` still authorizes), but the Livewire policy requires authorizing every public action.

`memberRole` is user input but has no `#[Validate]` attribute; it is validated with an inline `$this->validate([...])`, deviating from the project's `#[Validate]` + `$this->validate()` Livewire pattern.
No test asserts the required audit-log writes (`Log::channel('audit')`) for sending, cancelling, accepting or declining an invite.
The same new-feature bullet is added to both `[Unreleased]` and the released `[0.0.0]` section; a new feature must not be retro-added to a released changelog entry.
The admin/employee role `<select>` markup is duplicated between the invite form and the member modal; conventions favor extracting reusable markup into a Blade component.

review.summary: The change replaces direct member addition with an invite-only flow: `entity_invites` model/factory/migration, a queued localized invite mail, send/cancel on the members page, accept/decline on the switcher and onboarding, rate limiting, and a manager-only members page with detail and removal modals. It is close to complete and well tested, but needs changes: the invite-email validation error is not rendered explicitly, `openMember()` depends on an unverified `EntityMembership` `update` ability, and several mandatory project patterns (Actions for domain writes, policies for authorization, Livewire locking/validation) are not followed.
